stories.title: New York Investor Buys Palm Beach County Nursing Home for At Least $24M
stories.excerpt: Tordjman Equities has paid at least $23.8 million for a nursing home in Palm Beach County, property records show. Called Pine Trail Nursing and Rehab Center, the 59,760-square-foot facility features 93 beds at 4445 Pine Forest Drive in Greenacres, Fla., adjacent to South Military Trail. The Pine Trail facility was built in 1988 on an 8.7-acre property. The asset last traded for $3.5 million in 2004. An entity tied to K.C. Kross, the CEO of Oakland Park-based Mountaineer Development, served as the seller in the recent sale. The deed filed to Palm Beach County likely includes the value of only the real estate. The total price is probably higher to include the nursing home’s operating business and furniture. Pinnacle Bank, which merged with Synovus Bank in January, supplied a $150 million acquisition loan, serving as an administrator for a group of lenders. The debt backs another recent acquisition: the $16.6 million purchase of the 20,758-square-foot Westlake Nursing and Rehab Center in Dania Beach, Fla., earlier this month. Investors have been buying up senior housing assets across Palm Beach County as Florida’s senior population is projected to grow by 5.4 percent annually until 2031, and occupancy for those properties held steady at about 90 percent in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from Colliers. In August, Artemis Real Estate Partners purchased a relatively new assisted living facility in Delray Beach for at least $140 million from PGIM Real Estate. This month, Robbins Property Associates purchased a new housing community for residents 55 years and older in West Delray Beach for nearly $30 million. Representatives for Mountaineer Development and Tordjman Equities did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Tordjman Equities paid $23.8M for Palm Beach County nursing home; property value 6.8x since 2004.
Pinnacle Bank (Synovus) provided $150M acquisition loan covering two senior housing facilities.
Investor consolidation of senior housing across Palm Beach County signals florida demographic tailwinds.
stories.summary: Tordjman Equities acquired Pine Trail Nursing and Rehab Center (93 beds, 59,760 SF) in Greenacres for at least $23.8M, with the same lender funding a concurrent $16.6M acquisition of Westlake Nursing and Rehab in Dania Beach. The $150M acquisition loan from Pinnacle/Synovus backs both deals. The property has appreciated from $3.5M in 2004 to $23.8M today, reflecting strong institutional capital flowing into senior housing assets in Florida.
stories.impact: Senior housing consolidation and repricing in South Florida signals sustained in-migration of retirees and confidence in aging-population demand; however, this capital flow into senior facilities (not multifamily) may compete for institutional investors' attention and debt capacity in the South Florida market. The deal indicates lenders are willing to finance senior housing at scale, which could tighten capital availability for multifamily development in the region.

stories.title: Bath & Body Works to Open 9K-SF Store in Flatiron District
stories.excerpt: Bath & Body Works is opening a new store in Manhattan’s Flatiron District. The soap and scented lotion purveyor has signed a lease to take over the entire nearly 9,000-square-foot retail portion of 129 Fifth Avenue, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. Bath & Body Works will move into the two-level retail unit, owned by Acadia Realty Trust, in the fall of 2027, according to Crain’s New York Business, which first reported the lease. The eight-story building between East 19th and East 20th streets has 30 residential co-ops on its upper floors. The length of the lease and the asking rent were unclear, but a report from CBRE found retail rents along Fifth Avenue in the Flatiron District averaged $301 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026. Newmark’s Ariel Schuster and Michael Paster brokered the deal for the landlord, while Jeremy Ezra and Mai Shachi, also from Newmark, repped the tenant, according to Crain’s. Bath & Body Works seems to be replacing fashion retailer Express in its new Flatiron District space, though it’s unclear which other tenants have vacated 129 Fifth Avenue’s retail portion to make way for the new deal. Express signed a lease for only 5,000 square feet at the property in 2022. Bath & Body Works has at least 14 other stores in New York City across all five boroughs. One of those stores is at 304 Park Avenue South not too far from its new Fifth Avenue store, where the retailer sued SL Green Realty — that building’s landlord — in 2020 during the COVID pandemic to get out of its 2,500-square-foot lease. Bath & Body Works argued that an order from then-Gov. Andrew Cuomo to close all non-essential retailers in the state rendered its lease “no longer enforceable,” Commercial Observer reported at the time. It’s unclear whether the new lease represents a relocation from 304 Park Avenue South for the retailer. Isabelle Durso can be reached at idurso@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bath & Body Works leasing 9,000 SF at 129 Fifth Avenue (Flatiron) from Acadia Realty; opens fall 2027.
Flatiron Fifth Avenue retail asking rents averaged $301/SF in Q3 2026; flagship-scale retailer still committing.
Major retail operator securing long-term lease in prime Manhattan signals resilience in flagship retail demand.
stories.summary: Bath & Body Works signed a lease for nearly 9,000 SF across two levels at 129 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan's Flatiron District, with move-in scheduled for fall 2027. The building is mixed-use, with 30 residential co-ops above the retail space. Flatiron Fifth Avenue retail averaged $301/SF asking rent in Q3 2026. Newmark and Acadia Realty Trust brokered the deal.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. This is a retail lease renewal in a mixed-use building, signaling continued tourist and retail foot traffic in Flatiron—which supports residential demand in the neighborhood, but the article offers no new signals on multifamily fundamentals, supply, rents, or development feasibility in Manhattan.

stories.title: Marx Realty Secures Two Leases at 10 Grand Central
stories.excerpt: Marx Realty has secured two new leases at 10 Grand Central. Brenton Point will take 9,000 square feet on the building’s 24th floor and Cornerstone will occupy 5,000 square feet on the second floor of the hospitality-infused tower in the Grand Central neighborhood. “These leases reflect the range of top-of-line companies choosing 10 Grand Central and the beautiful experience we offer,” said Craig Deitelzweig, CEO of Marx Realty. “Brenton Point and Cornerstone will each benefit from an environment that brings together thoughtful design, highly personalized service and an extensive collection of hospitality-inspired amenities. We are excited to welcome both companies to the building.” Cornerstone was represented by Josh Pernice (CBRE) while Brenton Point was represented by Owen Reda and Gary Davies (CBRE). A JLL team of Mitchell Konsker, Thomas Schwartz, Carlee Palmer, and Margaux Kelleher represented Marx Realty. The property is 98% occupied. The post Marx Realty Secures Two Leases at 10 Grand Central appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marx Realty leased 9,000 SF (Brenton Point, floor 24) + 5,000 SF (Cornerstone, floor 2) at 10 Grand Central.
10 Grand Central hospitality-infused office tower now 98% occupied; two new office tenants inked.
Ongoing office leasing activity in Midtown Manhattan indicates selective tenant demand for amenity-rich space.
stories.summary: Marx Realty secured two office leases at 10 Grand Central: Brenton Point taking 9,000 SF on the 24th floor and Cornerstone occupying 5,000 SF on the second floor. The hospitality-infused tower is now 98% occupied. CBRE brokered both leases; JLL represented Marx Realty.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. This is an office leasing story in Midtown Manhattan's hospitality-office hybrid sector. No signals on multifamily demand, supply, or capital market conditions affecting residential development.

stories.title: RMR Lines Up $272M Mortgage Financing for Cedars-Sinai MOBs
stories.excerpt: The RMR Group Inc. has facilitated a $272.1-million interest-only mortgage financing secured by 8631 and 8635 W. Third St., two medical office buildings anchored by Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles. Morgan Stanley and BNP Paribas provided the financing. The loan has a two-year initial term with three one-year extension options and bears interest at one-month Term SOFR plus 180 basis points. Proceeds from the financing were used to repay approximately $267 million of existing mortgage debt scheduled to mature in February 2027 and to fund closing costs. The collateral consists of two 11-story medical office buildings totaling approximately 330,000 square feet, together with two structured parking garages, located on the campus of Cedars-Sinai Medical Center and connected to the hospital by skybridge. The portfolio is owned by a joint venture for which RMR provides asset and property management services. The primary owners of the venture are private institutional investors, and Diversified Healthcare Trust, an RMR client, owns a 20% equity interest. Hogan Lovells Cadwalader US LLP acted as counsel to the lenders and Sullivan & Worcester LLP acted as counsel to the borrower. Photo courtesy of ACCO Engineering Services. The post RMR Lines Up $272M Mortgage Financing for Cedars-Sinai MOBs appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: RMR secured $272.1M refinance (Morgan Stanley, BNP Paribas) for two Cedars-Sinai MOBs in Los Angeles.
Loan: SOFR+180bps, two-year initial term with three 1-year extensions; repaid $267M maturing debt.
Medical office at Cedars-Sinai campus (330K SF) holds 20% equity by Diversified Healthcare Trust (RMR client).
stories.summary: RMR Group facilitated a $272.1M mortgage refinance for two medical office buildings (330,000 SF total) anchored by Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles, provided by Morgan Stanley and BNP Paribas. The loan bears interest at SOFR+180 bps with a two-year initial term and three one-year extension options. Proceeds repaid approximately $267M of debt maturing in February 2027. Diversified Healthcare Trust (RMR client) holds a 20% equity stake.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. This is healthcare real estate (medical office buildings) financing and does not affect apartment supply, demand, or capital availability in the Los Angeles multifamily market, though it demonstrates lender appetite for institutional-quality real estate on healthcare campuses.

stories.title: JLL Arranges $20M Sale of Fully Leased 107K-SF Retail Center in Ohio
stories.excerpt: JLL arranged the $20.55 million sale of Hilliard Rome Commons, a 106,922-square-foot power center located at 1710 Hilliard Rome Road in Hilliard, Ohio. JLL represented the seller, RCG Ventures, LLC, in the transaction. CASTO acquired the asset. Built in 2002, Hilliard Rome Commons is a 100% occupied retail center anchored by Burlington, HomeGoods, Ulta Beauty, pOpshelf, Buffalo Wild Wings and a separately parceled Bank of America outparcel. The JLL Capital Markets team was led by Managing Director Michael Nieder and Director Brian Page. The center also features a diverse mix of complementary retailers, restaurants and service providers, creating a daily-needs and discretionary shopping destination for residents throughout the western Columbus metropolitan area. The property’s tenancy is supported by long-standing tenant relationships and a history of leasing momentum. “Investors were drawn to the combination of a fully leased center, a nationally recognized tenant lineup and a separately parceled Bank of America outparcel that provides future flexibility for ownership,” said Nieder. The post JLL Arranges $20M Sale of Fully Leased 107K-SF Retail Center in Ohio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL sold Hilliard Rome Commons (106,922 SF power center, 100% leased) in Hilliard, Ohio for $20.55M.
CASCO acquired retail center anchored by Burlington, HomeGoods, Ulta Beauty, pOpshelf, Buffalo Wild Wings.
Built 2002; strong tenancy and leasing momentum in western Columbus MSA supports retail buyer.
stories.summary: JLL arranged the $20.55M sale of Hilliard Rome Commons, a fully leased 106,922 SF power center in Hilliard, Ohio (western Columbus metro), anchored by Burlington, HomeGoods, Ulta Beauty, pOpshelf, and Buffalo Wild Wings. CASTO acquired the asset from RCG Ventures. The center was built in 2002 and features a separately parceled Bank of America outparcel providing future flexibility.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. This is a retail power center sale in Columbus, Ohio; no signals on residential demand, supply, employment growth, or development capital affecting the apartment sector.

stories.title: Sky Equity Taps Douglas Elliman for Sales at Upper East Side Luxury Condos
stories.excerpt: Sky Equity Group, the New York City-based real estate development firm founded by Simon Dushinsky, has named Douglas Elliman Development Marketing as the exclusive sales and marketing agent for 260 E. 72nd, the firm’s new luxury condominium on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. Located at the corner of Second Avenue and East 72nd Street, 260 E. 72nd will offer 60 two- to five-bedroom for-sale residences. Douglas Elliman Development Marketing is appointing luxury residential brokers Maya Kadouri as Director of Sales, along with Barbara Russo, Senior Sales Associate, and Gezelle Javaheri, Sales Agent, to lead sales at 260 East 72nd. The Peter Pennoyer Architects-designed 20-story building topped out in June and recently received Offering Plan approval, with pre-sales now underway ahead of the official sales launch later this fall. “Our goal for 260 East 72nd was to create a building that is rooted in the architectural character of the Upper East Side while being designed for the way people want to live today and for years to come,” said Dushinsky. “Maya, Barbara, and Gezelle understand this market and have the relationships and experience to represent a development of this caliber.” The post Sky Equity Taps Douglas Elliman for Sales at Upper East Side Luxury Condos appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sky Equity's 260 E. 72nd (Upper East Side, Manhattan) luxury condo: 60 units, topped out June, offering plan approved.
Douglas Elliman Development Marketing appointed exclusive sales/marketing agent; pre-sales underway, fall 2025 official launch.
20-story Peter Pennoyer Architects building, corner Second Ave & East 72nd; 2–5 bedroom for-sale residences.
stories.summary: Sky Equity Group's 260 E. 72nd, a 20-story luxury condominium on Manhattan's Upper East Side, has received Offering Plan approval and is beginning pre-sales ahead of a fall 2025 official launch. The building, designed by Peter Pennoyer Architects and located at the corner of Second Avenue and East 72nd Street, will offer 60 for-sale residences (2–5 bedrooms). Douglas Elliman Development Marketing is handling sales and marketing.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily rental development. This is a for-sale condominium conversion, not a rental apartment project. However, it signals sustained high-end residential demand on the Upper East Side and continued investor/owner-occupant appetite for Manhattan luxury residential product.

stories.title: DAUM Arranges Off-Market Deal for Santa Ana Warehouse
stories.excerpt: DAUM Commercial Real Estate Services has completed the off-market sale of a 29,932-square-foot Santa Ana industrial warehouse facility situated in Orange County’s Airport Area submarket. The price was not disclosed. EVPs Mike Barreiro and Devin Ray and associate Zack Homsy of DAUM’s Orange County office, along with EVP David Freitag and associates Ben Andrews and Sam Andrews of DAUM’s Los Angeles office, represented the seller and procured the buyer, an established global retailer and e-commerce wholesaler of currency collectibles and numismatic supplies, in the transaction. “The buyer serves collectors and customers around the world and will use the property as its new corporate headquarters,” saiidBarreiro. “The 20-foot clear height, oversized secured yard, dock-high and ground-level loading, and substantial electrical power gave them the infrastructure needed to support their growing e-commerce and distribution operations. Today, some of the best industrial property opportunities come down to relationships and knowing which owners are open to a conversation before a building ever hits the market.” The post DAUM Arranges Off-Market Deal for Santa Ana Warehouse appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: DAUM sold 29,932 SF industrial warehouse in Santa Ana (Orange County Airport Area) off-market; price undisclosed.
Buyer: established global e-commerce/numismatic retailer using property as new corporate HQ.
20-foot clear height, yard, dock-high loading, substantial electrical power support e-commerce + distribution.
stories.summary: DAUM Commercial Real Estate Services completed an off-market sale of a 29,932 SF industrial warehouse in Santa Ana's Airport Area submarket, Orange County. The buyer, an established global retailer and e-commerce wholesaler of collectible currency and numismatic supplies, will use the property as its new corporate headquarters. The facility offers 20-foot clear height, oversized secured yard, dock-high and ground-level loading, and substantial electrical capacity.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. This is an industrial/warehouse deal. However, it signals ongoing corporate relocations and e-commerce business expansion in Orange County, which could drive employment and population in-migration to the area—a secondary indicator of longer-term residential demand pressure in Southern California submarkets like Santa Ana and Irvine.

stories.title: PNC Lends $96M for Hawaii Retail Portfolio Acquisition
stories.excerpt: Aloha to permanent financing. 11North Partners has landed $96 million of acquisition debt for the purchase of a two-asset grocery-anchored retail portfolio in Lahaina, Hawaii, on the island of Maui. PNC Bank supplied the fixed-rate loan to facilitate the $155 million acquisition of the adjacent Lahaina Cannery and Lahaina Gateway properties from an affiliate of U.S. Realty Partners, according to Northmarq, which arranged the deal. “We are deeply honored to become the stewards of the Cannery Mall and Lahaina Gateway – two important legacy commercial properties in Hawaii. “This acquisition represents 11North Partners’ long-term commitment to serving the West Maui community and is our first entry into the Hawaii market,” Brian Harper, CEO o 11North Partners, said in a statement “For decades, these retail centers have served both locals and visitors in the region.” Northmarq negotiated the transaction with a debt and equity team consisting of Joe Giordani, Alex Kane and Matt Radich. The sale was facilitated by Northmarq’s Los Angeles investment sales team led by Bryan Ley and Tim Kuruzar, with Hawaii Commercial Real Estate’s Jamie Brown co-brokering the deal. “We ran a very competitive process across the lending landscape,” Giordani said in a statement. “The transaction highlights that banks continue to be highly competitive for well-structured, institutional-quality opportunities, particularly when they can pair attractive pricing with the flexibility of a customized, nonrecourse financing.” Situated across from each other on Hawaii Route 30, the properties net 5 million customers annually and benefit from a large-scale tourism economy in West Maui, according to Northmarq. Lahaina Cannery at 1221 Hawaii State Route 30 is more than 95 percent leased, anchored by Safeway and Longs Drugs. bullets: 11North Partners acquired Lahaina Cannery and Lahaina Gateway (two retail properties) for $155M; PNC provided $96M fixed-rate loan.
Grocery-anchored portfolio on Maui; 11North's first Hawaii market entry; Northmarq brokered.
U.S. Realty Partners seller; legacy retail properties serving West Maui locals and tourists.
stories.summary: 11North Partners secured $96M in acquisition financing from PNC Bank for a $155M purchase of two adjacent grocery-anchored retail properties—Lahaina Cannery and Lahaina Gateway—in Lahaina, Maui, Hawaii. This is 11North's first entry into the Hawaii market. Northmarq facilitated the transaction with fixed-rate financing. The seller was an affiliate of U.S. Realty Partners.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. This is a retail acquisition on Maui. However, institutional capital entering Hawaii retail (and 11North's market entry) may signal broader confidence in Hawaii tourism recovery and population/visitor demand post-pandemic, which could influence future multifamily development appetite in Hawaiian markets, though this deal provides no direct residential signals.

stories.title: One Street Secures $38M Loan for D.C. Office-to-Condo Conversion
stories.excerpt: One Street Commercial Properties has secured $37.8 million in financing to convert a vacant office building in Washington, D.C., into luxury condos. OakNorth and Hickory CRE Lending provided the loan for the redevelopment of 3333 K Street NW, a 70,000-square-foot former office building on the Georgetown waterfront. One Street acquired the property for $19 million in May 2025, records show. Built in 1988, 3333 K Street sits between the C&O Canal and the Potomac River. D.C.-based One Street plans to add a sixth floor and convert the property into 22 condominiums, including two affordable units, along with ground-floor retail space. Plans also call for a 24-hour concierge, valet parking, a fitness center, a swimming pool, and a resident lounge and club room. The financing adds another office-to-residential conversion to D.C.’s development pipeline while many obsolete office properties go underutilized since the pandemic. One Street has more than $250 million in assets under management and has completed more than $500 million in development over the past eight years, including adaptive reuse projects in the D.C. market. OakNorth has provided more than $23 billion in loans since it launched in 2015. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: One Street secured $37.8M financing (OakNorth, Hickory CRE) to convert 70,000 SF Georgetown office into 22 luxury condos.
3333 K Street NW: office-to-residential conversion, acquired May 2025 for $19M; adding sixth floor, ground retail.
Amenities: 24-hour concierge, valet, fitness, pool, resident lounge; two affordable units included.
stories.summary: One Street Commercial Properties secured $37.8M in financing from OakNorth and Hickory CRE Lending to convert 3333 K Street NW, a vacant 70,000 SF office building in Georgetown, Washington, D.C., into 22 luxury condominiums. One Street acquired the property for $19M in May 2025. The conversion includes a new sixth floor, ground-floor retail, and amenities (concierge, valet, fitness, pool, resident lounge). Two units will be affordable.
stories.impact: Office-to-condo conversion, not rental multifamily development. However, this signals (1) continued institutional lender appetite for residential conversions in Washington, D.C.; (2) adaptive reuse of obsolete office stock as a viable capital deployment strategy in D.C.; and (3) softness in office fundamentals driving selective conversion activity in prime submarkets like Georgetown. For multifamily developers, this suggests lenders are willing to finance conversion deals, which may compete with new construction for capital in the D.C. market and may reduce acquisition targets for future multifamily ground-up development.

stories.title: Eyewear Brand Gentle Monster Takes 29K SF at Kushner’s Puck Building
stories.excerpt: A luxury eyewear brand has its sights set on one of SoHo’s most high-profile retail vacancies. South Korean eyewear brand Gentle Monster has inked a 28,500-square-foot deal at the Kushner Companies’ Puck Building, Commercial Observer has learned. The lease term is more than 10 years, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. It’s unclear when Gentle Monster will arrive at 295 Lafayette Street, but it will take over a portion of the city’s much-mourned REI flagship, which spanned 35,000 square feet and ceased operations in July. The leftover portion of REI’s former space will be occupied by Italian restaurant Torrisi, which will expand its current 4,000-square-foot eatery at the base of the Puck Building, the source said. “We are incredibly excited to welcome Gentle Monster to the Puck Building,” Nicole Kushner Meyer, president of Kushner, said in a statement. “Puck is a special asset where heritage, modernism and culture come together, and we have been very intentional about bringing in brands and companies that share that same connection. “Gentle Monster’s creativity, global perspective and approach to experiential retail make them a natural fit for the building,” Meyer added. “This lease also marks an important milestone for us, completing the full transition of the Puck Building to an exceptional new generation of tenants while preserving the character and legacy that have always made it so iconic.” Puck Building. PHOTO: Courtesy Kushner Companies While Gentle Monster’s new space may seem unusually large for such a niche accessories brand, the Romanesque Revival office building may just be the eyewear maker’s perfect fit. Gentle Monster’s flagship stores are well known for their gallery-like designs and surrealist art installations. At the brand’s current SoHo location at 70 Wooster Street, for example, shoppers are greeted with massive, hyper-realistic robotic faces. bullets: Gentle Monster (South Korean eyewear brand) leased 28,500 SF at Kushner's Puck Building (SoHo) for 10+ years.
Filling portion of 35,000 SF REI flagship vacancy (closed July); Italian restaurant Torrisi expands adjacent 4,000 SF.
Luxury retail flagship committing long-term to high-rent SoHo submarket; flagship retail recovery signal.
stories.summary: South Korean luxury eyewear brand Gentle Monster signed a 28,500 SF lease at Kushner Companies' Puck Building (295 Lafayette Street, SoHo) for a term exceeding 10 years. The lease fills a portion of the 35,000 SF space vacated by REI's flagship, which closed in July. Italian restaurant Torrisi will occupy the remaining space and expand its existing 4,000 SF ground-floor location. The timeline for Gentle Monster's arrival is unclear.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. This is a flagship retail leasing story in SoHo. However, it signals recovery in luxury retail and flagship concept leasing in one of Manhattan's most prime commercial neighborhoods—a secondary indicator that SoHo remains an attractive submarket for high-end residential as well, supporting multifamily rental demand in the surrounding area, though no new pricing, supply, or development signals are provided.
